2: Filters run top to bottom; each read is counted once, at the first filter that removes it. Order: flag / no MM tags, chrM, rDNA, MAPQ < 20, aligned < 500 bp, qs < 10, then the outlier fence. MAPQ is the aligner's confidence in the placement: MAPQ = -10 log10(P(wrong place)), so 20 means a 1% chance the read is misplaced. qs is dorado's mean base quality of the read on the same scale: qs 10 means about 90% of bases are right. The reads are untrimmed, but the ~117 bp 5' adapter flank is soft-clipped by the aligner in 99% of reads, and it does not change MAPQ meaningfully: trimming and re-aligning 3,500 random reads moved 10 from below MAPQ 20 to above and 6 the other way (trim_check/analyze.out; trim_check/realign/compare.out, clipcut). Outlier fence: ONE pooled fence over all 7 barcodes (no longer one per run): median 0.0618, MAD 0.0223, fence median +- 4 x 1.4826 x MAD = [-0.070, 0.194], over 676,737 judged reads (>= 50 informative A calls). It removed 9,270 hypermethylated reads and 0 hypomethylated. By run: Mar20 1,067 (0.90% of reads before the fence); May07 2,591 (1.15% of reads before the fence); Jun25 5,612 (1.68% of reads before the fence). Kept 667,502 of 1,189,672 mapped reads (56.1% of reads, 72.5% of informative A calls). Sources: filtered_refit_nordna/filter_summary.tsv, fence.json, scripts/make_keep.py.
2b: Where: chrXII:451,418-468,929 holds two copies of a 9,137 bp rDNA unit in sacCer3; the real genome has about 150 copies in tandem (rDNA self-similarity scan, rdna_check/; checked here: sequence at x equals sequence at x + 9,137 over the whole 8,375 bp overlap, so the second copy is 8,375 bp and the last 762 bp of copy 1, chrXII:459,793-460,554, exist only once). Reads: 198,847 of 1,189,672 primary mapped reads overlap it (rdna_check/merged_*.rdna.tsv; filtered_refit_nordna/rdna_reads.txt). Share of all mapped reads by run: Mar20 17.0%; May07 16.9%; Jun25 16.4% (filter_summary.tsv). Depth 989.6x vs 52.5x for the rest of the genome in the merged pileup, 723.1x vs 51.6x in the filtered pileup (rdna_check/pileup_cov_rdna_vs_rest.txt). MAPQ: 131,546 rDNA reads at MAPQ 0, 58,230 at MAPQ 60; 68% of rDNA reads are MAPQ < 20 vs 4% of other nuclear reads (trim_check/analyze.out, class counts). 62,676 of the 63,707 MAPQ >= 20 rDNA reads touch the stretch present in only one reference copy (start + read length, rdna_check tsv), so their high MAPQ says they are unique in the reference, not that they come from one place in the cell. Methylation: pooled m6A 0.1066 rDNA vs 0.0649 rest (merged pileup; 0.0947 vs 0.0649 after filters). Median per-read rate among kept reads of the with-rDNA set (rdna_check/kept_rates.tsv.gz, >= 50 calls): 0.099 vs 0.061; by barcode rDNA vs rest: Mar20_bc01 0.097 vs 0.056; May07_bc03 0.083 vs 0.044; May07_bc04 0.082 vs 0.043; Jun25_bc21 0.113 vs 0.079; Jun25_bc22 0.108 vs 0.074; Jun25_bc23 0.111 vs 0.075; Jun25_bc24 0.111 vs 0.076. Before the fence, 15.6% of judged rDNA reads were above 0.18 vs 1.8% of other reads, with a tail to about 0.45 (99.9th percentile 0.394; 6 reads above 0.45). Hypothesis, not tested: a mix of open (transcribed) and closed rDNA copies. Among kept reads of the with-rDNA set, rDNA was 5.5% of Mar20, 6.6% of Jun25 and 8.6% of May07 reads, so it also differs by run. Fence: with rDNA in, 5,947 of 13,656 fence removals (43.5%) were rDNA reads though rDNA was 7.75% of judged reads; upper fence 0.2036 (filtered_refit/fence.json) -> 0.1940 without rDNA (filtered_refit_nordna/fence.json). Fitted rates (filtered_refit_nordna/fits/compare_fits.txt): background Watson 0.156480 -> 0.156354, nucleosome mean ratio 0.99771, all TF footprint means within 1.3%. No Chereji +-1 nucleosome and no Brogaard top-2000 dyad lies within 100 bp of the rDNA (checked on inputs/Chereji_2018_+1_-1_nucs.bed and the Brogaard bed); the TF fitting windows were not checked one by one. The small shifts come from the fence moving, which also drops some non-rDNA reads. Decoder: chrXII rDNA is where the old (non-log) decoder emitted invalid posteriors, up to 1e171 (CLAUDE.md gotchas; POSTERIOR_SCALING.md). Numbers computed by bg_investigation/nov03_final/rates_final.py -> rdna_checks.json.
H1: Pooled rates move by at most a few thousandths between read sets; linker rates hardly move at all. Brogaard cores and Chereji cores give the same ordering; Chereji cores read a little higher. The final row is the keep list used for the refit (rDNA excluded, one pooled MAD fence).
